Title: Vasoactive agents modulate migration of monocytes across glomerular endothelial cells.

Journal/Date: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research (2000)

--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: Macrophages seem to play an important role in the development of glomerulosclerosis. In both human and experimental animal models of focal glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), infiltration of macrophages in the mesangium has been considered key in the development of FSGS.
[METHODS]: In the present study, we evaluated the effect of vasoactive agents on the migration of monocytes across a filter in a modified Boyden chamber as well as across a cultured glomerular endothelial cell layer (in vitro model of glomerular mesangium). Both light as well as scanning electron microscopic studies were performed. We evaluated the effect of vasoactive agents including histamine, prostaglandin (PG) E2, angiotensin II, endothelin-1, platelet-activating factor, and interleukin-1 (IL) on the migration of monocytes/macrophages across an endothelial cell layer as well as a gelatin-coated filter. In addition, we evaluated the effect of cyclic adenosine 3',5' cyclic monophosphate (cAMP) and PGE2 on vasoactive-induced migration of monocytes.
[RESULTS]: Histamine increased (P < 0.003) the migration of monocytes across the filter. This effect of histamine was dose-dependent. Histamine at concentrations of 10(-8) to 10(-5) mol/L induced optimal migration across the filter (control, 16.6 +/- 1.1 vs histamine, 10(-8) mol/L, 40.9 +/- 0.9 monocytes/high power field). Cimetidine, an H2 receptor blocker, attenuated (P < 0.001) the effect of histamine on the migration of monocytes. PGE2 inhibited the migration of monocytes in a dose-dependent manner. Histamine increased (P < 0.001) the passage of monocytes across the glomerular endothelial cell layer (control, 1012 +/- 37 vs 1711 +/- 163 cpm/well). Histamine also increased the migration of murine macrophages across the glomerular endothelial cell layer. PGE2 inhibited the migration of monocytes across the endothelial cell layer under basal as well as histamine-stimulated states. Dibutyryl cyclic (DBc) AMP also attenuated the migration of monocytes under basal as well as histamine-stimulated states. Both PGE2 and DBcAMP also attenuated the IL-1 beta-stimulated migration of monocytes. Angiotensin II, endothelin-1, and platelet-activating factor did not modulate the migration of monocytes.
[CONCLUSIONS]: Vasoactive agents directly modulate the transmigration of monocytes. The present in vitro study provides a basis for a hypothesis that vasoactive agents may also be modulating the migration of monocytes across the glomerular endothelial cell layer (into the mesangium).

key_findings.finding: In the same direct glomerular-endothelial study (PMID 10736970), PGE2 inhibited monocyte migration dose-dependently across the filter and across the endothelial layer under basal and histamine-stimulated conditions; dibutyryl-cAMP likewise attenuated basal and histamine-stimulated migration. Both PGE2 and dibutyryl-cAMP attenuated IL-1β-stimulated migration, consistent with a cAMP-associated anti-transmigration/barrier or leukocyte-motility effect. Exact endothelial junctional/adhesion-marker measurements were not reported in the abstract.

source_tools.relevance: Abstract reports PGE2 and cAMP inhibition under basal, histamine-, and IL-1β-stimulated conditions

key_findings.finding: The same study found no modulation of monocyte migration by angiotensin II, endothelin-1, or platelet-activating factor in the tested assays. Thus, within this direct glomerular endothelial model, histamine was pro-transmigratory, PGE2/cAMP were inhibitory, and Ang II/ET-1 were null under the reported conditions.

entities.name: PMID:10736970
observations: Direct in-vitro study using cultured glomerular endothelial layers and gelatin-filter Boyden assays to measure monocyte migration.
Histamine increased migration; PGE2 and dibutyryl-cAMP inhibited migration; angiotensin II and endothelin-1 had no detectable effect under tested conditions.

source_tools.relevance: Primary direct evidence for vasoactive-agent effects on monocyte passage across glomerular endothelial cells.

entities.name: Histamine
observations: In cultured glomerular endothelial assays, increased monocyte passage dose-dependently; 10^-8 M increased filter migration from 16.6 ± 1.1 to 40.9 ± 0.9 monocytes/high-power field, and endothelial-layer passage from 1,012 ± 37 to 1,711 ± 163 cpm/well.
Cimetidine attenuated histamine-driven migration, supporting H2-receptor involvement.

observations: PGE2 inhibited monocyte migration dose-dependently across filters and glomerular endothelial layers, including basal and histamine-stimulated migration; it also attenuated IL-1beta-stimulated migration.
